job_description_info.job_description:
# Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity

**Company:** Corvale Mobility (fictional name; intercity rail and coach operator)
**Location:** Kraków, Poland (contract, remote-friendly; occasional office days)
**Engagement:** Service agreement (B2B / freelance), not an employment contract
**Rate:** 95 – 125 PLN per hour

## The engagement

Corvale is preparing a new generation of trains and needs a cloud infrastructure engineer for the team that links the vehicles to the company's cloud platform. You will help shape the architecture from the start and take it to production.

## Scope

- Design, build and operate the cloud infrastructure that links on-board train systems with backend services: telemetry ingestion, alerting, video streaming and remote content updates
- Maintain the infrastructure-as-code repository (Terraform with Terragrunt), keeping it tidy and approachable
- Lead technical proposals across backend and infrastructure from idea to production
- Contribute to system design and challenge decisions with arguments
- Set up secure train-to-cloud communication (mutual TLS, certificate management, network design)
- Agree interfaces and responsibilities with train manufacturers' engineers
- Support backend developers in deploying services that are easy to monitor and run
- Keep the platform observable, reliable and secure

## Requirements

- Hands-on infrastructure engineering and cloud environment design and operation
- AWS preferred; other major clouds acceptable
- Strong Terraform and Terragrunt
- Good understanding of systems architecture and system design
- Networking knowledge, including mTLS and SSL/TLS
- Practical security awareness
- Experience leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along
- Strong analytical thinking and clear communication

**Nice to have:** IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, backend or full-stack background (JVM preferred), Linux and virtual machines.

## Working model

Independent contractor, invoicing monthly for agreed services.

company_info.company_description:
Corvale Mobility is a privately held, founder-led transportation and software company headquartered in Kraków, Poland. It operates long-distance bus services and is expanding its passenger-rail network across Central Europe. Its asset-light model combines regional operating partners with Corvale’s own brand, route planning and digital booking platform, which offers trip tracking and other travel services. The company is investing in a new train fleet and prioritising greater use of data and machine learning.

Corvale describes itself as engineering-led and technology-first, with teams that take end-to-end ownership of their systems and work together to solve problems. Its stated values are **Lead, Shape, Own and Enjoy the journey**. It also highlights sustainability, shared goals across international teams, and opportunities for employees to shape their career paths.

Workplace feedback describes the culture as collaborative, fast-moving and open to new ideas. Corvale has received employee-survey-based workplace culture awards recognising areas including innovation, flexibility, purpose and values, professional development and appreciation. Technology roles may be available to employees or independent contractors; employee benefits include hybrid working and travel on the company’s network.

cover_letter_history.content:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to apply for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role at Corvale Mobility. I bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms on AWS, and a track record of taking platform initiatives from design and implementation through to production. Corvale’s need to shape a reliable, observable and secure foundation for connecting its new train fleet with cloud services is a strong match for my infrastructure and platform background.

In my current role as Senior Platform Engineer at Tallybrook, I lead a five-person platform team operating eight AWS EKS clusters across three regions, supporting approximately 350 services. I built an internal developer platform using service templates, Argo CD and Crossplane self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3, reducing the time to take a new service to production from around two weeks to under one day. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets for critical services, reducing weekly on-call pages by approximately 60%, and moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.

My earlier experience includes running AWS game-backend infrastructure for titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players, managing infrastructure through Terraform and Atlantis, and building an observability stack with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki. Across these roles, I have led technical work, supported service teams, and established practices that help systems remain operable in production. I would bring that experience to Corvale’s infrastructure design, Terraform repository, service deployment support and work with backend and manufacturer teams, while contributing clear, evidence-based thinking to system design decisions.

Corvale’s engineering-led approach and emphasis on end-to-end ownership resonate with the way I work: building dependable platforms that help teams deliver and operate services effectively. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform and platform engineering experience could support the Fleet Connectivity team.

Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved by inserting unsupported keywords.

The candidate's material does not establish Terragrunt, mTLS or SSL/TLS, certificate management, security engineering, train/vehicle connectivity, IoT or automotive integration, JVM/backend development, or explicit stakeholder engagement with external manufacturers. Linux experience is present in the original candidate information but is not surfaced in the letter. These are gaps or omissions, not reasons to make unsupported claims.
